research_question: In adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, do SGLT2 inhibitors compared with placebo reduce cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure?
note: Synthetic records for PROVIDER_MODE=fake. Trial names, authors, journals, identifiers, and numbers are invented. PMIDs use 991xxxxx, DOIs use the 10.5555 test prefix, and hosts use .example or .invalid.

records.title: Dapagliflozin versus placebo in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction: the CARDINAL-HF randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors may reduce heart failure events independent of glucose lowering. Methods: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 4812 adults with New York Heart Association class II to IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less were randomly assigned to dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily or placebo, in addition to guideline-directed therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure. Results: Over a median of 18.4 months, the primary outcome occurred in 391 of 2410 patients (16.2%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 509 of 2402 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.85; P<0.001). Hospitalization for heart failure occurred in 9.8% and 13.4%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.71). Serious adverse events related to volume depletion were uncommon. Conclusions: Among patients with heart failure and a reduced ejection fraction, dapagliflozin reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure compared with placebo.

records.title: Empagliflozin and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization in reduced ejection fraction: the EMBER-HF trial
records.abstract: Background: The effect of empagliflozin on outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction across the range of kidney function is uncertain. Methods: We randomized 3690 patients with chronic heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to empagliflozin 10 mg or placebo. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure. Results: During a median follow-up of 16 months, a primary outcome event occurred in 352 of 1846 patients (19.1%) in the empagliflozin group and 459 of 1844 (24.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.87). The annual decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate was slower with empagliflozin. Genital infections were more frequent with empagliflozin. Conclusions: Empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization in patients with reduced ejection fraction, regardless of diabetes status.

records.title: Sotagliflozin after worsening heart failure in patients with reduced ejection fraction: the SOLSTICE randomized double-blind trial
records.abstract: Background: Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibition might benefit patients recently hospitalized for heart failure. Methods: Patients with reduced ejection fraction were randomized before or within 3 days after discharge to sotagliflozin or placebo. The primary outcome was the total number of cardiovascular deaths and hospitalizations or urgent visits for heart failure. Results: Of 1222 patients enrolled, 608 received sotagliflozin and 614 placebo; the trial ended early because of loss of funding. The rate of primary outcome events was 51.0 vs 76.3 per 100 patient-years (rate ratio, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.85). Diarrhea and hypotension were more common with sotagliflozin. Conclusions: In patients with reduced ejection fraction after worsening heart failure, sotagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death and heart failure events compared with placebo.

records.title: Effect of dapagliflozin on symptoms and functional capacity in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the DEFINE-FUNCTION randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: Patient-reported outcomes matter in heart failure. Methods: This randomized, placebo-controlled trial assigned 263 patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to dapagliflozin or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) overall summary score. Results: The KCCQ overall summary score improved by 6.1 points more with dapagliflozin than with placebo (95% CI, 2.4 to 9.8). Six-minute walk distance improved by 21 m. There were too few cardiovascular deaths or hospitalizations for heart failure to compare. Conclusions: Dapagliflozin improved symptoms and physical limitations in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

records.title: Early in-hospital initiation of empagliflozin in acute heart failure: the EARLY-EMPA randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: Whether SGLT2 inhibitors can be started safely during hospitalization for acute heart failure is unknown. Methods: We randomized 530 patients hospitalized for acute heart failure, regardless of ejection fraction (median 38%), to empagliflozin 10 mg or placebo once stabilized. The primary outcome was a hierarchical composite of death, heart failure events, and symptom change at 90 days. Results: Patients assigned to empagliflozin were more likely to have a clinical benefit (win ratio, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.09 to 1.68). Death or first heart failure event occurred in 10.6% vs 14.7%. Conclusions: In-hospital initiation of empagliflozin in acute heart failure produced clinical benefit at 90 days and was well tolerated.

records.title: Canagliflozin in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes: a pilot randomized placebo-controlled trial
records.abstract: Background: Small mechanistic data suggested benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure. Methods: In this single-center pilot trial, 64 patients with type 2 diabetes and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction were randomized to canagliflozin 100 mg or placebo for 24 weeks. Results: Hospitalization for heart failure occurred in 2 of 33 patients with canagliflozin and 4 of 31 with placebo (P=0.42). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide fell by 18% with canagliflozin and 4% with placebo. Conclusions: Canagliflozin was well tolerated; the trial was not powered for clinical outcomes.

records.title: Ertugliflozin in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction: the ERTU-HF multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial
records.abstract: Background: Evidence for ertugliflozin in heart failure is limited. Methods: ERTU-HF randomized 2104 patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to ertugliflozin 15 mg or placebo. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure. Results: Over 20 months, the primary outcome occurred in 18.4% of the ertugliflozin group and 22.0% of the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68 to 0.97). Cardiovascular death alone did not differ significantly (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.71 to 1.14). Conclusions: Ertugliflozin reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization, driven by fewer hospitalizations.

records.title: Dapagliflozin in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction: the PRESERVE-D trial
records.abstract: Background: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce events in reduced ejection fraction, but their effect in preserved ejection fraction is less certain. Methods: We randomized 5988 patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction greater than 40% to dapagliflozin or placebo. Results: The primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death occurred in 16.1% vs 19.3% (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.94). Conclusions: Dapagliflozin reduced worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death in patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction above 40%.

records.title: Empagliflozin and left ventricular remodeling in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the EMPA-REMODEL cardiac magnetic resonance trial
records.abstract: Background: Reverse remodeling may explain benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors. Methods: Eighty-four patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less were randomized to empagliflozin or placebo for 36 weeks, with cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline and follow-up. Results: Left ventricular end-systolic volume index decreased by 16.6 mL/m2 with empagliflozin and 0.5 mL/m2 with placebo (difference, -16.1; 95% CI, -23.1 to -9.1). Ejection fraction increased by 6 percentage points. Conclusions: Empagliflozin produced reverse left ventricular remodeling; clinical outcomes were not assessed.

records.title: Sex differences in the effect of dapagliflozin in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a prespecified analysis of the CARDINAL-HF trial
records.abstract: Background: Women are underrepresented in heart failure trials. Methods: We compared the effect of dapagliflozin versus placebo on the primary outcome by sex among the 4812 CARDINAL-HF participants, of whom 1131 (23.5%) were women. Results: The hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.59 to 1.00) in women and 0.74 (95% CI, 0.64 to 0.86) in men (P for interaction=0.81). Conclusions: Dapagliflozin reduced the risk of worsening heart failure and cardiovascular death similarly in women and men.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitor use and heart failure hospitalization in reduced ejection fraction: a nationwide cohort study
records.abstract: Background: Trial results may not generalize to routine care. Methods: Using a national heart failure registry, we identified 21 480 patients with an ejection fraction of 40% or less; 6230 started an SGLT2 inhibitor. Propensity score overlap weighting balanced 42 covariates. Results: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.80) and cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95) over 2 years. Conclusions: In routine care, SGLT2 inhibitor use in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction was associated with fewer hospitalizations, consistent with trial evidence.

records.title: Real-world adherence and outcomes of dapagliflozin in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a multicenter registry analysis
records.abstract: Background: Adherence to SGLT2 inhibitors outside trials is unknown. Methods: A prospective registry at 38 centers followed 3115 patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction who started dapagliflozin. Results: At 12 months, 81% remained on treatment. Discontinuation was associated with a higher risk of hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.81). Conclusions: Most patients persisted with dapagliflozin; stopping treatment was associated with more heart failure hospitalizations.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitor initiation at hospital discharge and one-year mortality in heart failure: a propensity-matched cohort
records.abstract: Background: Discharge is a key moment to start therapy. Methods: In a propensity-matched cohort of 4404 patients discharged after hospitalization for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, we compared patients prescribed an SGLT2 inhibitor at discharge with those who were not. Results: One-year all-cause mortality was 12.1% vs 15.9% (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.88); readmission for heart failure was 21.4% vs 26.0%. Conclusions: Discharge initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors was associated with lower mortality and fewer readmissions; residual confounding is possible.

records.title: Kidney function trajectories in patients with heart failure starting empagliflozin: a retrospective cohort
records.abstract: Background: An early dip in kidney function can lead clinicians to stop SGLT2 inhibitors. Methods: We studied 2870 patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction who started empagliflozin. Results: Estimated glomerular filtration rate fell by a mean of 3.8 mL/min/1.73 m2 in the first 4 weeks and then stabilized; an early dip greater than 10% was not associated with heart failure hospitalization or death. Conclusions: The initial decline in kidney function after empagliflozin is usually benign and should not prompt discontinuation.

records.title: Ketoacidosis and genital infections with SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure: a pharmacovigilance cohort
records.abstract: Background: Safety signals for SGLT2 inhibitors come mainly from diabetes populations. Methods: We linked prescription and hospital records for 9762 patients with heart failure who started an SGLT2 inhibitor. Results: Diabetic ketoacidosis occurred at 0.9 per 1000 person-years, almost entirely in patients with diabetes; genital mycotic infections occurred at 21 per 1000 person-years. Conclusions: Serious adverse events with SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure were rare.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
records.abstract: Background: Several trials have tested SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Methods: We searched three databases to March 2023 for placebo-controlled randomized trials. Results: Five trials with 12 838 patients were included. SGLT2 inhibitors reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.70 to 0.82; I2=0%), hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.70), and cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.86). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors consistently reduce heart failure events and cardiovascular death in reduced ejection fraction.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitors across the ejection fraction spectrum: an individual participant data meta-analysis
records.abstract: Background: It is unclear whether the benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors varies with ejection fraction. Methods: We pooled individual data from 21 947 participants in four placebo-controlled trials. Results: SGLT2 inhibitors reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.83), with no heterogeneity by ejection fraction category (P for trend=0.57). Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure events across the full range of ejection fraction.

records.title: Mechanisms of benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure: a narrative review
records.abstract: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure events through mechanisms beyond glucose lowering. This review summarizes natriuresis and decongestion, improved myocardial energetics, reduced fibrosis, and kidney protection, and discusses how preclinical findings in rodent models relate to outcomes in clinical trials of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitors: a new pillar of therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: In this editorial, we argue that the consistent reduction in cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure across trials justifies SGLT2 inhibitors as a fourth foundational therapy alongside renin-angiotensin inhibitors, beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.

records.title: Comparative efficacy of foundational therapies for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a network meta-analysis
records.abstract: Background: Four drug classes reduce events in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Methods: Network meta-analysis of 69 randomized trials with 91 741 patients. Results: Compared with placebo, comprehensive therapy with an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor had the largest reduction in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 0.39). SGLT2 inhibitors added to other therapy reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure by about one quarter. Conclusions: Quadruple therapy offers the greatest benefit.

records.title: Empagliflozin attenuates cardiac fibrosis in a mouse model of pressure-overload heart failure
records.abstract: Male C57BL/6 mice underwent transverse aortic constriction and received empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day) or vehicle for 4 weeks. Empagliflozin reduced interstitial fibrosis by 38%, preserved fractional shortening, and lowered expression of profibrotic genes. These findings suggest that SGLT2 inhibition limits adverse remodeling in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

records.title: Dapagliflozin improves myocardial energetics in a rat model of ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: Rats with myocardial infarction induced by coronary ligation were randomized to dapagliflozin or vehicle for 8 weeks. Dapagliflozin increased myocardial ketone oxidation and ATP production, improved ejection fraction from 31% to 38%, and reduced heart weight. SGLT2 inhibitors may improve cardiac energetics in heart failure.

records.title: Euglycemic ketoacidosis after dapagliflozin initiation in a patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a case report
records.abstract: We describe a 61-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction who developed euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis 9 days after starting dapagliflozin, during a period of reduced oral intake. He recovered with intravenous fluids and insulin. Clinicians should counsel patients to pause SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness.

records.title: Rationale and design of the CARDINAL-HF trial of dapagliflozin in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: CARDINAL-HF is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that will test whether dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduces cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in about 4800 patients with an ejection fraction of 40% or less. Randomization uses a central interactive web response system stratified by diabetes status. This article describes the design, endpoints, and statistical analysis plan.

records.title: Dapagliflozin in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: comment on the CARDINAL-HF trial
records.abstract: We question whether the benefit of dapagliflozin in CARDINAL-HF applies to patients already taking sacubitril-valsartan, who made up only 11% of the trial population, and ask the investigators to report outcomes in this subgroup.

records.title: Cost-effectiveness of dapagliflozin for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in five European health systems
records.abstract: Background: Payers need evidence on value. Methods: A Markov model using CARDINAL-HF efficacy estimates projected lifetime costs and quality-adjusted life-years for dapagliflozin added to standard care. Results: The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio ranged from 7200 to 11 900 euros per quality-adjusted life-year. Conclusions: Dapagliflozin is likely cost-effective for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in Europe.

records.title: Empagliflozin and glycemic control in type 2 diabetes without heart failure: a 52-week randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: SGLT2 inhibitors lower glucose in type 2 diabetes. Methods: We randomized 986 adults with type 2 diabetes and no history of heart failure to empagliflozin or placebo added to metformin. Results: HbA1c fell by 0.7 percentage points more with empagliflozin; body weight fell by 2.1 kg. Hospitalization for heart failure was rare in both groups. Conclusions: Empagliflozin improved glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

records.title: SGLT2 inhibition and progression of chronic kidney disease: the KIDNEY-SHIELD randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: Patients with chronic kidney disease are at high risk of kidney failure and heart failure. Methods: We randomized 4304 patients with chronic kidney disease, with or without diabetes, to an SGLT2 inhibitor or placebo. Results: The primary kidney composite occurred in 9.2% vs 14.5% (hazard ratio, 0.61). Hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death was reduced by 29%. Conclusions: SGLT2 inhibition slowed kidney disease progression.

records.title: Sacubitril-valsartan versus enalapril in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a randomized trial
records.abstract: Background: Neprilysin inhibition may add to renin-angiotensin blockade. Methods: We randomized 8102 patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction to sacubitril-valsartan or enalapril. Results: Cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure occurred in 21.6% vs 26.2% (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.87). Conclusions: Sacubitril-valsartan was superior to enalapril.

records.title: Statin therapy and incident heart failure in older adults: a population cohort study
records.abstract: Background: Statins prevent atherosclerotic events, but their effect on heart failure risk is unclear. Methods: We followed 52 300 adults aged 75 years or older without heart failure for 6 years. Results: Statin use was associated with a lower risk of incident heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.81 to 0.95) and cardiovascular death. Conclusions: Statins may lower heart failure risk in older adults.

records.title: Vericiguat in patients with worsening heart failure and reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: Background: Soluble guanylate cyclase stimulation is a new approach to heart failure. Methods: We randomized 5050 patients with reduced ejection fraction and a recent worsening heart failure event to vericiguat or placebo. Results: Cardiovascular death or first hospitalization for heart failure occurred in 35.5% vs 38.5% (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82 to 0.98). Conclusions: Vericiguat modestly reduced heart failure events.

records.title: Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose in iron-deficient patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: Background: Iron deficiency is common in heart failure. Methods: We randomized 1108 iron-deficient patients with reduced ejection fraction after hospitalization for heart failure to intravenous ferric carboxymaltose or placebo. Results: Total heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death were reduced by 21% (rate ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.62 to 1.01). Conclusions: Iron repletion may reduce heart failure hospitalizations.

records.title: Dapagliflozin vs Placebo in Patients With Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: The CARDINAL-HF Randomized Trial
records.abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors may reduce heart failure events independent of glucose lowering. Methods: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 4812 adults with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less were randomly assigned to dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily or placebo. Results: The primary outcome of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure occurred in 391 of 2410 patients (16.2%) with dapagliflozin and in 509 of 2402 patients (21.2%) with placebo (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.85). Conclusions: Dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

records.title: Empagliflozin and Cardiovascular Death or Heart Failure Hospitalization in Reduced Ejection Fraction (EMBER-HF)
records.abstract: We randomized 3690 patients with chronic heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to empagliflozin 10 mg or placebo. A primary outcome event of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure occurred in 19.1% of the empagliflozin group and 24.9% of the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.87).

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
records.abstract: Five trials with 12 838 patients were included. SGLT2 inhibitors reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.70 to 0.82) with no heterogeneity.

records.title: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin and total worsening heart failure events in reduced ejection fraction: a pooled trial analysis (preprint)
records.abstract: We pooled CARDINAL-HF and EMBER-HF to study total (first and recurrent) worsening heart failure events in 8502 patients with reduced ejection fraction. SGLT2 inhibitors reduced total heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular deaths (rate ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.83). This preprint has not been peer reviewed.

records.title: 2023 focused update of the guideline for the management of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
records.abstract: The writing committee recommends an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) for all patients with symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, regardless of diabetes status, to reduce cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure (class I, level of evidence A). Therapy should be started early, including before discharge.

records.title: CARDINAL-HF: dapagliflozin versus placebo in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction | Cardiovascular Therapeutics Reports
records.abstract: Among 4812 patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less, dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure compared with placebo (16.2% vs 21.2%; hazard ratio, 0.75).

records.title: Diabetes drug cuts heart failure hospitalizations by a quarter, trial finds
records.abstract: A large trial presented this week found that dapagliflozin, originally developed for diabetes, reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure by 25% in people with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Experts called the result practice changing.

records.title: Dapagliflozin prescribing information: heart failure indication
records.abstract: Dapagliflozin is indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Recommended dose is 10 mg once daily. Warnings include ketoacidosis, volume depletion, and genital mycotic infections.

records.title: Started an SGLT2 inhibitor for my heart failure - my experience
records.abstract: I have heart failure with an ejection fraction of 30% and my cardiologist added empagliflozin six months ago. I feel less breathless and have not been back in hospital, but I needed to pee a lot at first. Has anyone else noticed a difference?
